A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AR-AT research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support comparison. Earlier material can be matched despite substantial appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original AR-AT experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Imagenette, including component ablations, representation analyses and hyperparameter studies.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds component diagnostics, repeated-run results, AR-AT+SWA evaluations, L2-bounded experiments and computational-time measurements.

M1.justification: The core stop-gradient, predictor, split-BN, automatic loss balancing and multilayer regularization procedures remain unchanged. v3 adds an optional combination with stochastic weight averaging, AR-AT+SWA, in Section 5.2 and Table 3. This is a limited procedural extension rather than a redesign of AR-AT.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Imagenette for image classification. v3 Appendix B.4 adds L2-bounded adversarial training and evaluation on both CIFAR datasets, extending the threat scenarios beyond the earlier L-infinity setting without adding datasets or application domains.

E2.justification: v3 substantially expands the reported comparator set while retaining earlier baselines. Tables 11-12 add NuAT2 and NuAT2+WA on CIFAR-10, TRADES+HF on CIFAR-100, and AT+HF, TRADES+Rand and TRADES+AWP+Rand on both datasets. These entries are explicitly identified as results copied from prior papers, rather than newly reproduced experiments.

E3.justification: The default 100-epoch training schedule, PGD-10 training attacks, PGD-20/AutoAttack evaluation and dataset splits remain unchanged. Additional protocols include training-perturbation sweeps, L2 attacks with epsilon 0.5, batch-size diagnostics spanning 128-1024, and AutoAttack-based component comparisons. The original PGD-20 component table is retained as Table 15. The new L2 comparison uses PreAct ResNet-18 for AT and ResNet-18 for AR-AT.

E4.justification: v3 directly tests mechanisms previously supported more indirectly: Figure 2 isolates the two stop-gradient directions, Figures 3-4 examine feature divergence and predictor stability, Appendix E tests batch-size sensitivity, and Appendix F analyzes feature separation and BN running-statistic stability. Component ablations also extend across both CIFAR datasets and architectures. Earlier layer, loss-weight and component studies remain present.

E5.justification: v2 reports point estimates for benchmark accuracies without repeated-run counts. v3 Table 3 reports means and standard deviations over five runs for LBGAT and AR-AT variants, substantially strengthening uncertainty reporting for the principal comparisons. This establishes newly reported repetition, not an increase from a known earlier run count. Table 19 also introduces timing variability.

E6.justification: Principal estimates change and substantial new results appear. For CIFAR-10/WRN-34-10, v2 reports AR-AT clean/AA accuracy of 90.81/51.19; v3 Table 3 reports five-run means of 90.89/50.77 and adds AR-AT+SWA at 90.06/54.03. New L2, mechanism, comparator and runtime results broaden the findings. Imagenette results and several earlier ablations remain unchanged. Appendix Tables 11-12 are not fully reconciled with Table 3's updated estimates.

T1.justification: v3 corrects Equation 1 to distinguish the adversarial example x + delta from the optimizing perturbation. Equation 5 adds a factor of one-half to the stop-gradient decomposition. These are local mathematical revisions; the new explanatory appendices do not introduce a substantial theorem or proof framework.

C1.justification: Both versions identify gradient conflict and mixed BN statistics as central obstacles, propose AR-AT to improve the robustness-accuracy trade-off, and connect these mechanisms to knowledge-distillation defenses. v3 emphasizes understanding and broader empirical support, but these changes do not materially redefine the central scientific claims. The conclusion retains the same claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds a substantive explanation for component interaction: stop-gradient weakens invariance regularization and can exacerbate clean/adversarial feature separation, explaining its dependence on split-BN. Appendix E interprets persistence across batch sizes as evidence of distribution-wide conflict, while Appendix F develops the BN-statistics explanation. The existing limitations concerning layer selection and architectures without BN remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly identifies cross-entropy as the adversarial-example generation loss, adds a single-A100 timing protocol and per-batch resource measurements, and promises code release upon publication. Existing optimizer settings, predictor dimensions, dataset details and baseline implementation links are retained. The attack-loss statement is additional disclosure; SWA-specific implementation settings remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting SWA, the trade-off metric and additional defenses: Izmailov et al., Sitawarin et al., Sriramanan et al., Jin et al. (2023), and Li et al. Existing positioning relative to TRADES, MART, knowledge distillation and split-BN remains substantially intact. The author-year citation conversion is a presentation change.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around understanding invariance regularization, and Section 5.1 is reorganized into a more detailed component-analysis narrative. Earlier appendices are regrouped into experimental-details and performance-comparison sections, alongside new explanatory appendices. v3 also adds acknowledgments, ethics and reproducibility statements and adopts the ICLR document style.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 2 as a two-panel diagnostic, adds feature-divergence, predictor-stability, trade-off, batch-size and BN-statistics plots, and expands table structures for uncertainty and SWA results. The original component table moves to Appendix B.5, while earlier UMAP, parameter-sharing and Asym-TRADES figures remain. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering and numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens previously indirect support for the central mechanisms through isolated-loss, predictor-stability and BN-statistics diagnostics. Five-run uncertainty reporting and broader comparator coverage also make the empirical claims more assessable. These gains outweigh remaining weaknesses: incomplete SWA implementation details, unreconciled main-text/appendix results, and an architecture mismatch in the new L2 comparison. The improvement rests chiefly on stronger evidence and analysis, rather than higher reported performance.
